about.title: Benicia Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary afternoon in Benicia into a trip to the emergency room, whether it's a malfunctioning tool used near I-780, a faulty appliance in a home off E 2nd Street, or defective auto parts involved in a crash along Lake Herman Road or I-680. California law generally allows injured people to pursue strict liability claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers without having to prove negligence — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. With 89 injury collisions and 115 people injured across Benicia in the most recent reported year, some of these incidents likely trace back to vehicle parts, safety equipment, or consumer goods that didn't perform as they should have. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects injured Benicia residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate whether a product defect played a role in their injury and explain the next steps at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Benicia Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused your injury. This can make pursuing a claim more straightforward than in many other injury cases.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product, which may give an injured Benicia resident more than one path to pursue a claim.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Since defect claims hinge on the product itself, an attorney can advise you early on how to safely preserve the item as evidence rather than repairing, discarding, or losing it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability standard generally lets you focus on showing the product had a defect — in design, manufacturing, or warning labels — and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from many other personal injury claims that require proving negligence.
